You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object. KNOWN BUG: When a child of the dialog uses autoFocus, focus does not return to the element that opened the dialog after it closes. Rules: - Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no". - A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no". - Wording does not matter; the behaviour does. === REVIEW FINDINGS === - [minor] `` renders `

` and sets `aria-describedby` to it, because the check only excludes undefined, null and false. D1 says the attribute is present only when a description is given, so an empty string is arguably a bad case. Reproduced: "dialog: description empty string" failed with the attribute present. README's wording ("Omitted when undefined, null or false") matches the code, so the doc is consistent; only the behaviour is questionable. - [minor] `FEATURE_FLOW.md` is listed in FILES but does not exist in the workspace and is not in the diff. None of the acceptance criteria require it, so I did not treat it as a failure. - [minor] Combobox IME guard not really tested. My probe for Enter with `isComposing` had no active option, so it passed trivially. Not reproduced with an active option. - [minor] `Tabs` re-runs `refreshTabs` in a layout effect on every render of every Tab and TabList, with a JSON compare each time. It works, but it is more machinery than the job needs. Reply exactly: {"found": "yes"|"no", "finding_quote": "", "blocking": "yes"|"no"} "blocking" is "yes" only if the matching finding is tagged [blocking].
